final_answer:
Depth-First Search (DfS) and Breadth-First Search (BfS) are traversal algorithms for graphs. DfS explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, using a stack (or recursion). BfS explores all neighbors at the current depth level before moving deeper, using a queue.  

DfS is suitable for problems like finding connected components, detecting cycles, or exploring paths in mazes (e.g., solving puzzles). It uses less memory for deep, narrow graphs. BfS is optimal for finding the shortest path in unweighted graphs (e.g., social network friend recommendations) or when all nodes at a certain depth must be processed together. It uses more memory for wide graphs but guarantees the shortest path in unweighted cases.  

Choose DfS for deep exploration or limited memory, and BfS for shortest-path problems or level-based processing.
